result.summary:
Gated docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-023.md (branch feature/WF02-REQ-023, commit 5673c14) independently. Read core-directives.md, WF-02 Step 3b, docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md in full (all 7 stated ACs plus AC8/S10, AC-schema, AC-catalog, and the design's own §0/§2/§3/§5/§6 mechanism sections), apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts's isAutoPromotionHalted, apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible, apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts's confirm callback and sendPromotionNotification, then the test spec file itself end to end -- not TEST-DESIGNER's own claims about it.

Coverage check: every AC (AC1-AC8, including the boundary sub-case AC2-boundary) plus AC-schema and AC-catalog has at least one verification case with an exact command, exact fixture SQL/TS, exact expected value, and an explicit Pass/FAIL condition. No 'TODO' found anywhere in the file (grepped, zero hits). No case relies on subjective judgment -- every expected value is a literal outcome kind (e.g. {kind:'capacity-full'}), a literal SQL predicate/count, a literal catalog string, or an exact sendMessage/audit-row count.

AC2 boundary verified directly against source (task step 3): apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts line 744-746 reads exactly `return startsAt.getTime() - evaluationTime.getTime() <= AUTO_PROMOTION_HALT_WINDOW_MS;` with AUTO_PROMOTION_HALT_WINDOW_MS = 24*60*60*1000 -- confirms the halt is inclusive of exactly T-24h, matching the spec's claimed boundary rule verbatim (spec even cites the correct line number and comparison operator). The spec's three test instants -- exactly T-24h (expect true), T-24h-minus-1-second i.e. 24h+1s remaining (expect false), and T-24h+1s i.e. 23h59m59s remaining (expect true) -- correctly straddle both sides of the <= boundary: one instant strictly greater than the threshold (not halted), the exact threshold instant itself (halted, the load-bearing off-by-one check), and one instant strictly inside the halt window (halted, for contrast). This exercises the boundary correctly on both sides via a pure function call with millisecond control, plus a separate live-dispatch corroboration that correctly caveats it cannot guarantee literal microsecond precision at the dispatch level (honest scope statement, not overclaiming).

AC4 iteration-count judgment (task step 4): the spec's 5-iteration dispatch-level case is a NEW multi-actor configuration (capacity=3, 2 concurrent withdrawals x 2 concurrent registrations, 4-way contention for 2 freed seats, all via real bot.handleUpdate) not previously exercised anywhere -- BACKEND-DEV's own domain-level test only covers a single promotion vs a single fresh registration, at 20 iterations, via direct function calls. Judged sufficient, not requiring a rework increase, for two structural reasons the spec itself states and I independently verified against the code: (1) the property under test (Postgres's FOR UPDATE lock on the shared events row serializing all contending transactions, design SS3.1) is the SAME lock-acquisition mechanism regardless of how many transactions queue on it -- a 2-vs-2 race exercises the identical serialization primitive as the already-20x-tested 1-vs-1 race, just with more waiters queued on the same lock, not a qualitatively different mechanism needing independent statistical confidence; (2) the existing 20-iteration domain-level test already accumulates statistical confidence in the core claim (never over-admits) at low cost (direct function calls), while this spec's 5 iterations add a materially different, higher-fidelity configuration (real dispatch, real handler code including resolveActingUser/decideWithdrawOutcome paths the domain-level test bypasses) whose main incremental value is exercising the full stack under contention, not incrementally more statistical assurance of the lock itself. The spec also names an honest secondary confidence check (winner-variety across iterations) and correctly scopes it as non-blocking. I consider 5 adequate here specifically because it is additive to an existing 20x direct-call test of the same underlying lock, not a replacement for it -- if this were the ONLY concurrency test for this property, 5 would be too low for a hard gate.

AC7 structural argument verified directly against source (task step 5): apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts line 140-141 has exactly one call site for sendPromotionNotification, gated on `outcome.kind === "withdrawn" && outcome.promotion.kind === "promoted"` (grepped the whole file -- one match). Traced apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible (lines 361-421+) directly: step 2 (admittedRows count) and the seatsLeft computation are freshly re-queried from the DB on every call, not cached or memoized -- so a second call against an event the first call already refilled to capacity recomputes seatsLeft as 0 and decidePromotionEligibility's row 3 (seatsLeft <= 0) returns {kind:'capacity-full'} before step 4 (candidate selection) is ever reached, exactly as design SS5 claims. A {kind:'capacity-full'} result can never satisfy the `=== 'promoted'` guard, so the second run structurally cannot trigger sendPromotionNotification regardless of what calls it. This is a sound, independently re-derived structural argument, not merely a restatement of the design doc's own claim.

Cross-checked exact expected values against the real implementation (task step 6): AUTO_PROMOTION_HALT_WINDOW_MS/isAutoPromotionHalted's comparison operator (above), the sendPromotionNotification call site and its guard condition (above), and the AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC7 domain-level test describe() label strings the spec cites (grepped apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts: 'REQ-023 AC1' at line 859, 'REQ-023 AC2' at 903, 'REQ-023 AC3' at 940, 'REQ-023 AC4' at 962, 'REQ-023 AC5' at 1029, 'REQ-023 AC7' at 1076 -- all match the spec's cited line numbers) and apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.test.ts ('REQ-023 AC6' at 319, 'S10 rework' at 392 -- both match). No invented test name, no stale line reference.

No mocked/stubbed grammY Context anywhere (task step 7): every case in this spec is either a pure function call (isAutoPromotionHalted), a direct domain-function re-run pointer to BACKEND-DEV's existing DB tests (which the prior REQ-022 gate already confirmed use a real grammy Bot instance, no mocked Context), or this spec's own live-dispatch cases which explicitly reuse the REQ-020/021/022-established harness (real Bot instance, bot.handleUpdate, captured sendMessage array, real Postgres via docker compose) -- confirmed by the Shared Setup section's explicit instruction to reuse that harness verbatim and its explicit reference to grammY's real Context.api binding semantics (SS6.2) rather than any substitute.

Failure-mode statement check (task step 8): every AC section (AC1, AC2/AC2-boundary, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC-schema, AC-catalog) ends with explicit 'Pass conditions' and a named FAIL condition describing the exact regression it exists to catch (e.g. AC2-boundary: 'a run returning false for the exact T-24h instant is a FAIL'; AC7: 'a run where the second call promotes anyone, writes any audit row... is a FAIL'; AC4: 'any iteration where the admitted count... is not exactly 3... is a FAIL'). None left implicit or deferred to TEST-RUNNER's judgment. The coverage table at the end cross-references every AC against its verification and an explicit 'Would fail if violated?' column, all answered Yes with a concrete violation description.

No check failure found. PASS.
